body.aasraya_basis: Aasraya yogas are based on the signs occupied by planets. If all the planets are in movable signs or in fixed signs or in dual signs, these yogas arise.
body.adhi_example_note: Section 11.3.6's example places the Moon in Taurus and the benefics in Virgo and Leo, which are the 5th and 4th from Taurus. The rule asks for the 6th, 7th and 8th. The rule is followed.
body.chandra_intro: Chandra yogas are the lunar combinations. There are several yogas based on Moon.
body.combustion_is_a_qualifier_not_a_veto: Section 11.2.4 says a yoga formed by a combust planet loses “some of their power to do good”, not all of it. A combust yoga is therefore reported as present with a qualifier, never suppressed.
body.combustion_note: If Mercury is too close to Sun, he is combust (asta or astangata). Yogas formed by combust planets lose some of their power to do good.
body.frequency_note: Because Mercury and Venus are with Sun or a sign away from him most of the time, the following yogas are very common in rasi chart. However, they are less common in divisional charts. One can apply these yogas in D-9 and D-10 in particular.
body.hamsa_name_note: Section 11.4.5's Definition calls the yoga “Ruchaka”, which is Mars's yoga from section 11.4.1. The heading reads “Hamsa Yoga” and is followed — see docs/book-deviations.md D-30.
body.kemadruma_effort_note: One with this yoga has to work hard and succeed through great efforts.
body.kemadruma_is_a_qualifier_not_a_veto: Section 11.3.4 says Kemadruma kills the *results* of other good yogas, not the yogas themselves. A yoga forming beside it is reported present with a qualifier, never suppressed.
body.kemadruma_kills_other_yogas: This bad yoga kills the results of other good yogas in the chart, especially Chandra yogas.
body.mahapurusha_element_role: Pancha mahapurusha yogas produce five kinds of great persons with one of these 5 elements playing a predominant role in their personalities.
body.mahapurusha_element_rulers: Mars, Mercury, Saturn, Venus and Jupiter (respectively) represent these 5 elements.
body.mahapurusha_intro: Pancha mahapurusha yogas give the combinations that produce 5 kinds of great persons.
body.mahapurusha_reference_rule: This yoga does not apply from Moon and it applies mainly in rasi chart.

naabhasa_classification.basis: the natures of the planets occupying the quadrants

body.naabhasa_gap_note: Section 11.5 classifies 32 Naabhasa yogas and sections 11.5.1 and 11.5.2 define five of them. The other 27 — the Aakriti and Sankhya families — are named only. They are listed here rather than registered, so that a yoga the engine cannot detect never appears among the verdicts where its absence would read as a finding.
body.naabhasa_intro: Naabhasa yogas are classified celestial combinations.
body.naabhasa_timing_rule: Results of other yogas may be felt primarily during the dasas of the planets and signs involved. But the results of Naabhasa yogas are felt in all dasas.
body.node_note: Three of the four Ravi yogas turn on “a planet other than Moon”. Chapter 11 never says whether Rahu and Ketu count as “a planet”, so it is a per-call choice and the nodes are excluded by default. See docs/open-items.md OI-73.
body.ravi_intro: Ravi yogas are the solar combinations. There are several yogas based on Sun.
body.results_note: The results each yoga gives are PVR's own prose and are withheld from this response under the licence gate of OI-12.
body.sarpa_is_very_bad: This is a very bad combination.
body.sun_excluded_note: The Sun cannot form a yoga about what accompanies him, so he is excluded from his own houses alongside the Moon.

timing_example.text: Suppose someone has Sun and Mercury together in Leo in D-10. Then that person has a powerful Budha-Aditya yoga in career. The results will be felt throughout one's life and the periods of Sun, Mercury and Leo will give those results in particular.
